Let \(a=-x,\ b=-y,\ c=-z\). Then \(a,b,c\ge 0\) and
\[
a=b^2+c^4,\qquad b=c^2+a^4,\qquad c=a^2+b^4.
\]
If \(M=\max(a,b,c)\), say \(M=a\), then \(b=c^2+a^4\ge a^4\), and since \(b\le a\), we get \(a^4\le a\), so \(a\le 1\). Thus \(0\le a,b,c\le 1\).

Let \(t\) be the positive root of \(t^3+t-1=0\), so \(2/3<t<3/4\). Define
\[
A=\frac{3t^2}{2t-3}<0.
\]
For any \(u\in[0,1]\),
\[
u^3-t^3\le A(u-u^2-u^4).
\]
Indeed, after multiplying by \(2t-3<0\), the difference factors as
\[
(2t-3)\bigl(A(u-u^2-u^4)-u^3+t^3\bigr)
=(u-t)^2\bigl(-3t^2u^2+(4t-3)u+(2t^2-3t)\bigr)\le 0.
\]
Thus the inequality holds.

Applying this to \(a,b,c\) and summing,
\[
a^3+b^3+c^3-3t^3
\le A\bigl((a+b+c)-(a^2+b^2+c^2)-(a^4+b^4+c^4)\bigr)=0,
\]
because summing the transformed system gives
\[
a+b+c=(a^2+b^2+c^2)+(a^4+b^4+c^4).
\]
So
\[
a^3+b^3+c^3\le 3t^3=3(1-t)<1.
\]
Hence
\[
x^3+y^3+z^3=-(a^3+b^3+c^3)\in(-1,0].
\]
Therefore the minimum possible floor is \(-1\), attained at \(x=y=z=-t\). Thus \(m=-1\), and
\[
m\equiv -1\equiv 2006 \pmod{2007}.
\]

\boxed{2006}
